SEC-7: the write/GC audit's fencing findings (J1/J2/J3) are attacker-amplifiable — an attacker who can skew a victim's clock via unauthenticated NTP can force a premature mount-lease reclaim and induce split-brain (J3), and an attacker who can induce a long stop-the-world pause (resource exhaustion, cgroup throttling) widens the unfenced `mayMutate()` to `casPut` window for a zombie write (J1); TLS protects S3 transit but NTP is typically unauthenticated. Recommendation: carry `writer_epoch` into the shard-CAS precondition, and require authenticated time (NTS/authenticated NTP) in deployment guidance.

Writable Store::open validates server_root_id, claims the owner, allocates a durable writer epoch, validates the CAS request budget, claims the mount lease, starts MountLeaseKeeper, and arms the mount fence.
The owner object at gc/server-roots/<srid>/owner rejects a foreign UUID and rejects re-claiming an absent owner over a non-empty data subtree with CORRUPTED_DATA.
writer_epoch is allocated from gc/server-roots/<srid>/epoch by a durable CAS bump and is strictly increasing across crashes and restarts.
A live mount lease stores MountLease{server_uuid, writer_epoch, hostname, pid, started_at_ms, seq, expires_at_ms, min_active, gc_fenced}.
Before discovery, `computeHeartbeatFloor` fences out expired writer mounts so their last commits are durable before the LIST sweep.
Heartbeat classification uses `live`, `terminated`, and `expired`; an expired non-terminated mount is fenced with a token-guarded overwrite that preserves its body and sets `gc_fenced`.

The three server-root control objects live under `gc/server-roots/<srid>/`: `owner` is a write-once identity anchor, `epoch` is a CAS-bumped monotone counter, and `mount` is a token-guarded lease body.
`server_root_id` must be non-empty, at most 255 bytes, contain no empty, `.` or `..` path segment, and not use reserved `_files` or `_manifests` segments; invalid IDs fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.
The mount heartbeat's `min_active` field records the oldest in-flight `build_seq`, while `UINT64_MAX` is the farewell or retired sentinel.

GC fence-out of an expired lease and the Store's local write-fence are distinct mechanisms: GC persists `gc_fenced=true`, while Store latches local `lost` and gates ordinary ref mutations through `mayMutate()`.
A GC-fenced `(uuid, epoch)` mount cannot be refreshed in place; recovery must allocate a fresh writer epoch.
A same-UUID, same-epoch fenced mount yields `FencedSelf`, a foreign owner yields `ForeignOwner`, and a same-UUID live different epoch yields `LiveDoubleStart` from `claimMount`.
A hard-killed server's stale mount is waited out for at most the lease TTL plus margin before reclaim, while a live twin causes `LiveDoubleStart` and aborts.
When a running server detects that GC fenced its mount, it latches the local write fence, schedules remount, and retries with a fresh epoch without throwing from the remount loop.

The mount model requires sticky server-root ownership, a durable monotone writer epoch, and observation-based reclaim over a stable holder token for a full TTL-plus-drift window on the reclaimer's monotonic clock.
Mount reclaim must not trust the foreign mount body's wall-clock timestamp and must install the successor's own mount body.
The per-write mount guard is a pure local check `!lost ∧ now < deadline`; superseded writers are blocked by the sticky local `lost` latch rather than a per-write shared-state read.
The writer mount fence is the monotone `writer_epoch` stored at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/epoch`, and a fencing failure is reported as a recoverable `MountFencedException`.
Each writer renewal uses one `PUT` carrying both the mount lease and the build watermark `min_active`, plus one `gc/state` `GET` for the current round.
The heartbeat floor phase costs one `LIST` of `gc/server-roots/`, N server-root `GET`s, and only rare token-guarded fence-out `PUT`s for expired mounts.
Every durable write or delete captures the mount fence generation at admission and rechecks it immediately before the object-store call and on every conditional retry; reads are not fence-gated.
The server-root owner object is never deleted or reassigned; it binds `server_root_id` to one `server_uuid`, and an absent owner over a non-empty owned subtree fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The object `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount` carries both the liveness lease and build watermark, including `writer_epoch`, renewal `seq`, `expires_at_ms`, `min_active`, and `gc_fenced`.
The local mount fence uses `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, not `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, so a VM resumed from suspend observes the elapsed lease deadline.
GC classifies a mount with `gc_fenced` as already fenced and a mount with `min_active == UINT64_MAX` as cleanly terminated; fencing preserves the body and uses token-guarded `putOverwrite`.
The mount lifecycle writes a terminal farewell with `min_active = UINT64_MAX` only after a certified drain; if the drain is not certified, no farewell is written.
A writer advertises `observed_gc_round` only after every in-flight `mutateShard` started under the older view has received its CAS response.

`Store::refreshViewForBeat` loads `gc/state` and retired-list objects before swapping the view under an exclusive `view_gate`; any read failure leaves the current round unchanged so the acknowledgement cannot advance.

The writer beat holds a shared `view_gate` lock across the entire `mutateShard` operation, and `Store::open` loads the retire view before starting the keeper so the first heartbeat acknowledges the loaded round.

The heartbeat floor excludes terminated mounts using `min_active == UINT64_MAX`, fences expired-unfenced mounts with token-guarded overwrite, and re-reads on a fence-out precondition failure before classifying the entry.

The merged heartbeat body carries the existing mount fields plus `min_active_build_seq`, `observed_gc_round`, and `gc_fenced`; `observed_gc_round` is monotone and `gc_fenced` is terminal for the incarnation.
If `gc/state` is unavailable during a writer heartbeat, the writer does not advance its GC acknowledgement but still renews its lease; this can stall deletion globally without taking writers down.
Writable open ordering is claim heartbeat, load `gc/state` and the retired list, stamp `observed_gc_round`, and only then enable mutations.

An expired heartbeat without a terminated stamp is fenced out with a token-guarded overwrite that sets `gc_fenced` and bumps `seq`; successful fence-out makes the sleeper's next renewal fail and excludes it from the acknowledgement floor.

A mount created during a GC pass either participates in the enumerated heartbeat floor or, if pagination misses it, loads a view at least as new as the last published round before its creation and therefore sees every entry eligible for graduation.

A fence-out is terminal for an incarnation but a live server can self-remount by creating a fresh incarnation; `Store::tryRemountOnce` repeats the durable epoch bump, `claimMountAwaitingExpiry`, retired-view load, and write-fence arming, while older-epoch builds fail closed with `ABORTED`.

`claimMountAwaitingExpiry` retries the unchanged `claimMount` only for a same-UUID `LiveDoubleStart`; it immediately returns `ForeignOwner`, returns `Claimed` after token-guarded reclamation, and returns `LiveDoubleStart` after the bounded wait expires.

The mount-reclaim wait deadline is latched from the first stale lease's `expires_at_ms` plus a margin and capped at no more than one TTL plus margin from the wait start; no new user setting is introduced.
Mount reclamation is safe because `claimMount` overwrites the observed mount token conditionally; a live holder that renews between observation and reclaim changes the token and cannot be stolen.

`Store::open` calls `claimMountAwaitingExpiry` after bumping `writer_epoch`; it logs the first wait and throws the existing `ABORTED` double-start error only for a foreign owner or a lease that remains live through the wait bound.
`HeartbeatFloor` gains `max_ack`, computed from every decoded mount body including fenced and terminated bodies, because the rebuild needs the maximum observed acknowledgement to mint a safe round.
The mount-recovery plan requires a zero poll interval to be raised to a one-millisecond floor so the bounded wait cannot spin indefinitely.
`mayMutate` is checked on every flush attempt; if the fence trips, the whole batch fails with `ABORTED` and no caller receives a successful mutation.
The queue leader holds the shared side of `view_gate` for the entire flush, so a batch remains one in-flight mutation for the beat and drain protocol.

A clean restart of both servers with 10,000 tables recovered all tables in 64.2 seconds, with no unknown-disk false positives and `CasBlobList=0` at startup; the rapid-kill S13 wedge is not a normal graceful-restart failure.
`Cas::listMounts` enumerates mount slots with one LIST and one GET per slot and classifies each as `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.

The planned `system.content_addressed_mounts` table has columns `disk`, `srid`, `server_uuid`, `hostname`, `pid`, `writer_epoch`, `seq`, `started_at_ms`, `expires_at_ms`, `min_active`, `observed_gc_round`, `gc_fenced`, and `state`.

Mount-slot audit adds `CasEventType::MountClaim`, `MountRelease`, and `MountConflict`, serialized as `mount_claim`, `mount_release`, and `mount_conflict`; conflict details include the observed holder UUID, hostname, PID, epoch, sequence, and expiry when available.

`Store::observedGcRound()` returns the currently installed `retire_view.round()` through the retired view's internal synchronization, so renewal performs local reads and one lease PUT without a `gc/state` GET.

The retired-view syncer runs `syncRetiredView()` every `mount_renew_period`, performs the `gc/state` probe and `RetireView::refresh()` only when the published round is newer, and emits `RetiredViewAdvance` only for an actual advance.

Both the lease-renewal thread and retired-view syncer are gated by `background_watermark`; `Store::open` and `tryRemountOnce` synchronously call `syncRetiredView()` before starting the keeper so the first anchored lease carries a current acknowledgement.

The retired-view syncer catches and logs its own exceptions, retries on the next tick, and must be stopped and joined before `retire_view` or `pool_backend` are destroyed; renewal fail-closed behavior otherwise remains unchanged.
Terminating a never-started `SingleWriterSlot` is a quiet no-op, while double termination of a genuinely started slot remains an exception.
`MountClaimResult::FencedSelf` represents a same-UUID, same-epoch mount body with `gc_fenced=true`; `claimMount` must not write a refresh in that case, and a different epoch may reclaim immediately.

`Store::open` retries fence recovery at most three times; on `FencedSelf` or `MountFencedException` it allocates a fresh writer epoch, rebuilds the keeper, and retries, while the final `armMountFence` uses the final epoch.

After a successful mount claim, `doStart` retains one synchronous view refresh before the first lease body; the renewal background path itself is a single lease PUT and the view refresh runs on its own cadence.
`Store::renewWatermarkOnce()` remains the composed test/manual driver that runs `syncRetiredView()` and then `mount_keeper->renewOnce()`, while production renewal uses the isolated cheap path.
`Store::observedGcRound() const` returns `retire_view.round()` as a cheap, race-safe in-memory read, and `renewLeaseOnlyForTest()` renews without synchronizing the retired view.

The Store-owned retired-view syncer exposes `startRetiredViewSync`, idempotent `stopRetiredViewSync`, and `retiredViewSyncLoop`; it waits on a condition variable, catches and logs body exceptions, and is joined during Store teardown.
A mount body with `gc_fenced = true` is terminal for its `(server_uuid, writer_epoch)` incarnation; recovery must use a fresh `writer_epoch`.
`MountLeaseKeeper::claim` must refuse adoption of a fenced body when the observed UUID and epoch equal the current incarnation, and the caller must recover as a new incarnation.
The same-UUID/same-epoch refresh branch of `claimMount` must also refuse a fenced body; only a different epoch may reclaim it.
A foreign `server_uuid` causes a fail-closed refusal, while an own UUID with `gc_fenced` is a recoverable fence state and an own UUID with a newer unfenced epoch is a fail-closed supersession.
`prepareRenew` must be O(1) and use the last installed `retire_view.round()` acknowledgement plus `minActive()` without running the beat; the beat runs on a separate cadence.

`Store::open` must wrap claim and keeper startup in a bounded retry loop; an adoption refusal classified as `fenced_by_gc` allocates a fresh epoch and retries, while foreign or superseded refusals abort.
`SingleWriterSlot::doTerminate` is a quiet no-op when `seq == 0`, because a keeper whose start never succeeded has nothing to release; double termination remains an exception.

A fence-recovery implementation must classify same-UUID fenced bodies as recoverable, decouple the beat from the renewal deadline, retry cold-open claim/adopt, and make `doTerminate` with `seq == 0` a no-op.
The P3.1 fence-recovery cycle recovered a fenced ch1 mount in about two seconds as `writer_epoch=2`, `seq=1`, `gc_fenced=0`, and `state=live`, with no post-kill foreign-writer or exit-49 lines.
CA metadata `startup()` and `shutdown()` are idempotent, allowing the base disk and cache disk to share one CA mount and one lease when they reuse the same metadata storage.

The writer-side `RetireView`, its syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed; `MountLease` loses `observed_gc_round`, the beat publishes only `{now, min_active}`, and GC round recovery no longer uses `min_ack` or `max_ack`.

The writer records an exact precommit removal before retiring a failed build, while a newly mounted writer fences the predecessor epoch and appends one constant-size epoch clear per affected namespace.
A writer does not retire a build while it owns a precommit; if the process stops first, only a successor that fenced the entire predecessor epoch may append the namespace-scoped epoch clear.

`WriterId` is `{ writer_epoch, writer_sequence }`, both components are nonzero `UInt64` values, each successful mount strictly increases `writer_epoch`, and `writer_sequence` starts at one within an epoch.
A current-build precommit removal requires the build to remain locally active until the exact removal record is durable; the replay transition is not liveness-dependent.

Writable startup fences the predecessor, verifies the exact adopted fold seal, installs its `RefBaseSet` metadata, and lazily loads each namespace by reading its base rows and replaying its complete tail between before/after `gc/state` checks.

For a current-writer failure, the writer keeps the build active, appends the exact precommit removal, and retires the build only after that removal is durable; if the append fails, the build remains active and the error propagates.
Artifact keys are pinned to `attempt = lease.seq`, and renew or steal paths bump `lease.seq` every round, so a same-key collision can only be a byte-identical resend within the same attempt.

`RefTxnId` is `{ writer_epoch: UInt64, ref_sequence: UInt64 }`; both fields are nonzero, writer epochs strictly increase on successful mounts, and `ref_sequence` is strictly increasing within a mounted writer epoch.
Namespace recreation after `remove_namespace` requires the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker for the exact removal transaction; an empty physical prefix is not sufficient.
The writer consumes only the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker as the namespace cleanup completion signal; a physically empty prefix is not authoritative.
If a mount lease expires, the writer is fenced and a subsequent staging-source 404 must fail closed by aborting the insert rather than committing.
The staging sweeper exposes `sweepOwnMountOnStart()` and `ageSweep(now, ttl)`, both lease-fenced so an in-flight staging object younger than TTL is not deleted.

CAS separates `attempt_timeout`, `operation_deadline`, and the local `lease_deadline`; a writer attempt requires an unfenced mount, `now < lease_deadline`, `now + attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin < lease_deadline`, and `now + attempt_timeout <= operation_deadline`.
`lease_safety_margin` accounts for local scheduling delay, timeout granularity, and configured clock-skew allowance, but does not bound server-side completion after a client timeout.

A writer updates its cache and returns ACK only after a fence check, one controlled S3 attempt, permitted resolution, and a final fence check; if the final check fails, it returns no ACK and reports uncertainty when the object may exist.

Writable startup validates effective timeout, operation, safety-margin, renewal-period, and lease-TTL relationships before making the mount writable; invalid settings do not silently fall back to generic S3 defaults.
`Store::~Store` must latch a shutdown flag before joining `remount_thread`, `scheduleRemount` must refuse to spawn after that flag is set, and teardown must re-join after `mount_keeper->stop()`.
`MountLeaseKeeper` must join its renewal thread in `~MountLeaseKeeper()` before its `std::function` callbacks are destroyed.

`Store::openForDecommission` must impersonate the victim `server_root_id`, bump `writer_epoch`, start a lease keeper, throw `ABORTED` when the member is alive, and throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` when neither an owner anchor nor a mount body exists.

`Cas::decommissionPoolMember` returns a `DecommissionReport` containing namespace, committed-ref, precommit, edge-delta, manifest-debris, staging, mountpoint, slot-removal, and warning fields; non-empty `warnings` means the slot is retained.
Decommission emits the `CasEventType::MemberDecommission` event under the string name `member_decommission` for begin, per-namespace, and end events.

Decommission's staging and roots sweeps use paged LIST plus exact-token deletion; any per-object exception, `TokenMismatch`, or `NotFound` is recorded as a warning and the slot is kept as the resume anchor.

The SQL surface is `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER '<srid>' FROM DISK '<disk>'`; the AST carries the srid in `query.replica` and the disk in `query.disk`, and the interpreter returns a one-row report result.

The SQL decommission command leaves the executing server's own mount untouched by creating a separate admin claim of the victim srid over the same backend, executes synchronously, and returns the report as a one-row result set.

Observation-based reclaim waits for a stable mount token for `TTL + Drift` on the reclaimer's clock before advancing the durable epoch; the reclaim installs the successor's fresh-epoch, unfenced mount body rather than leaving the old body in place.

Observer-side death decisions in rev.6, including `GcFence` and `ClearExpiredMount`, must use `mount.deadline + Drift <= clock`; the holder-side `Write` check remains `clock < fenceUntil`, and the deliberate `WallClockReclaim` sabotage is retained only to detect unsafe wall-clock trust.

`claimMount` never reclaims a same-uuid, different-epoch lease solely because its wall-clock deadline passed; it returns `LiveDoubleStart` unless the lease is `gc_fenced`, carries the clean marker `min_active == UINT64_MAX`, or the caller supplies a matching proven-dead token.

A clean store shutdown sets `shutting_down`, waits for ref queues and leaders to settle within the request budget, and writes the farewell marker only when no unresolved conditional PUT wedge remains; otherwise it stops the lease keeper without a terminal farewell.
A self-remount pays `materialization_grace_ms` only when `refLanesSettledForRemount` finds an unresolved wedge; a settled remount skips the grace and does not mark `unclean_epoch_boundary_seen`.
The writer's lease-liveness checks use local zero-request `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` fences through `mayMutate` and `refAppendFenceOk`.
A `gc_fenced` lease is a transferable certificate of observed death, so a successor may skip token observation and pay only `materialization_grace_ms`.
A clean lease release drains all ref-append lanes and writes `released_clean` only after every in-flight conditional PUT resolves within the ordinary request budget.
If clean-release draining leaves an unresolved PUT at the shutdown deadline, the `released_clean` marker is skipped and the successor treats the handover as unclean.
Unclean takeover observes a stable lease token for `mount_lease_ttl_ms * 1.05 + poll_interval_ms` on the observer's monotonic clock before reclaiming with token-guarded `putOverwrite`.
A durable reader pin at `gc/readers/<reader_id>` contains per-namespace `base_snapshot` and `tail_head` values plus `lease_expiry`.
Reader pins are pool-global, heartbeated, republished at reader start, and ignored by GC after the reader lease expires.
`decodePoolMeta` rejects a pool with `min_reader_generation` above `G_BUILD` or a generation below `kRefSnapshotLogGeneration` with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

The server-root text objects are `cas_owner`, `cas_epoch`, and `cas_mount_lease`: the owner binds a server-root id to a server UUID, the epoch stores the monotone next writer epoch, and the mount lease stores the live holder and merged `min_active` state.
A `MountLease` uses `UINT64_MAX` in `min_active` as the retired farewell sentinel, and `gc_fenced` is a terminal GC fence-out flag.
The proposed fetch-pin reaper used the existing `min_active` build-watermark floor from `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, not a wall-clock TTL.

The mount-lease protocol is fail-closed: another writer cannot claim a slot until the current lease expires, so continuing to write while `now < lease_deadline` is safe unless a proven supersession has occurred.

The implementation plan adds `SingleWriterSlot::shouldFenceOnTransientRenewFailure()` as a protected virtual hook defaulting to `true`, with `MountLeaseKeeper` overriding it for deadline-aware retry behavior.
`MountLeaseKeeper` refreshes its confirmed lease deadline on both successful `claim` paths and every successful background renewal.
The new `MountLeaseKeeper` `lease_safety_margin_` constructor parameter is appended after the existing `event_sink_` parameter and has a default of 2000 milliseconds, preserving existing call sites.
Production `CasMountRuntime::installKeeper` passes `cas_request_budget.lease_safety_margin_ms` to `MountLeaseKeeper`.

The source-layout rename verification required the counts of `build_seq`, `buildSeq`, `BuildPrefix`, `allocateBuildSeq`, `active_build_seqs`, `next_build_seq`, and `inflight_builds` to remain unchanged across the `Build`→`PartWriteTxn` rename.
Decommission must inspect every `DeleteOutcome`, abort the tail on any non-`Deleted` result, and delete mount before the claimed epoch and owner so successor objects cannot be reclaimed.
The decommission tail must delete the farewell mount token first, then the epoch token captured under the claim, and owner last; every non-`Deleted` result aborts the tail and retains the slot.

Mount leases and epoch counters already use exact-token deletion plus rechecks, but `OwnerObject` contains only `server_uuid`, so an owner anchor written by a successor reclaiming the same `srid` is indistinguishable from stale debris from the decommissioned server.

The decommission tombstone preserves the same `server_uuid`, sets `retired_at_ms` to the current time, and writes it with the prior owner token through `Backend::putOverwrite(owner_key, encodeOwner(...), owner->token)`.

The recovery retry loop releases `rt.state_mutex` before sleeping and re-acquires it afterward; this avoids stalling the whole-store `wedgedRefLaneCount` walk, and the default sleep is interruptible when `fence_ok_fn()` becomes false.
A proposed shared `checkNotReadOnly` helper is intended to guard all four mutating CAS entry points: transactions, GC round, GC rebuild, and pool-member decommission.
Clean termination after the mount lease object has vanished is a no-op release and must not throw `LOGICAL_ERROR`; a present foreign incarnation remains a genuine logic error.

`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage::startup` should build the pool, facade, capability result, and scheduler in locals and publish `cas_store`, `part_access`, `pool_uuid`, `conditional_copy_supported`, and `gc_scheduler` in one final pointer-mutex section; a startup exception must publish nothing.
The explicit CAS lifecycle states are `Mounted`, `Unmounting`, and `Dormant`, with the startup publish step entering `Mounted`.
`poolAccess` must acquire `pointer_mutex` once, reject non-`Mounted` or missing-pool states with `INVALID_STATE`, and otherwise return a coherent pool plus part-access snapshot.
`unmountSynchronously` is idempotent and resumable: it gates new operations, stops the GC scheduler, drains outstanding pool snapshots, and leaves the disk in `Unmounting` if its timeout expires.
`mountExplicitly` is idempotent from `Mounted`, performs a fresh startup from `Dormant`, and rejects a concurrent or incomplete `Unmounting` state with `INVALID_STATE`.
`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED UNMOUNT <disk>` must refuse to unmount while any loaded table references the disk's metadata storage, including cache-wrapper disks sharing that storage.

A dormant CA disk answers read-only existence and enumeration probes as absent: `existsFile` and `existsDirectory` return false, `isDirectoryEmpty` returns true, and listing/iteration is empty; `getFileSize`, non-IfExist object retrieval, and mutating operations still throw.

The `system.content_addressed_mounts` columns `srid`, `pid`, `seq`, and `min_active` are renamed to `server_root_id`, `process_id`, `renewal_sequence`, and `min_active_build_sequence`; `started_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` remain unchanged.
A mounted CAS disk couples all pool use, including reads, to a live mount lease and heartbeat; using the pool without them violates the mount contract.
A CAS disk is cached forever in the process disk registry by `Context::getOrCreateDisk`, so it has no clean teardown or runtime reset path.

A full-prefix LIST can prove pool emptiness only on a backend with documented strongly consistent prefix LIST semantics and only after the required settle/grace window and repeated samples; Local, Emulated, unqualified S3-compatible gateways, and RustFS without evidence have no natural proof.
CAS disk use is through untracked `shared_ptr` holders, so `use_count` cannot reliably determine whether a disk is unused or identify who holds it.
A lease-loss callback is untyped and cannot distinguish foreign fencing, transient deadline expiry, an absent mount key with intact data, and confirmed backing destruction.
A sound CAS lifecycle must use typed health states, fail-loud data-bearing enumeration outside a proven `Vanished` state, and reserve benign-absent answers for `Vanished` only.
A CAS disk stop must hand pool teardown to a thread other than the keeper callback thread and serialize scheduler shutdown through `gc_scheduler_mutex`.

`IdentityLost` is terminal: it is entered only after authoritative `KeyAbsent` for both `_pool_meta` and the owner-claim key, the remount thread exits, matching-sentinel restoration does not revive it, and recovery requires restart or `FORGET`.
`Vanished(replaced)` is established by a single transient-recovery comparison showing `_pool_meta` present with a foreign `pool_id`.
The rev.8 `Vanished(forgotten)` error states that `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` decommissioned the disk, that erasure was not verified, and that a restart re-registers the name.
`ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, `Indeterminate`, and mixed probe results never produce terminal conclusions; they keep the pool transient and retry.
`ProbeOutcome` distinguishes `Present`, `KeyAbsent`, `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, and `Indeterminate`; transport errors must never be flattened into `KeyAbsent`.

Every durable CAS PUT, DELETE, and staging finalize captures the fence generation at admission and throws typed error 668 before the backend call if mutation is no longer allowed or the generation changed; the check repeats before each conditional retry.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED FORGET` must publish terminal intent, trip the mount fence, stop renewal without clean release unless ref lanes are drained, stop GC, join keeper/remount/GC threads outside `remount_mutex`, and then enter `VanishedForgotten`.

For a same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced mount body, `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` with state-uncertainty diagnostics and relies on fencing plus self-remount rather than constructing `LOGICAL_ERROR`.
For a same-uuid body with a different writer epoch, `onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` as the normal superseded fencing outcome and reports `superseded by a newer incarnation`.

A foreign-uuid mount body remains a deliberate `LOGICAL_ERROR`-loud invariant violation because the owner anchor makes foreign claims protocol-unreachable; the classifier does not take over the mount.
If the mount-slot object vanishes during renewal, the keeper throws `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`, stops renewing, and fails closed without aborting or re-minting.
The renewal keeper samples separate wall and `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` anchors before I/O, passes the boot anchor to `on_renew_ok`, and computes each deadline as its own attempt-start anchor plus TTL.

When materialization grace consumes the claim TTL, startup must perform exactly one fresh conditional lease write before arming the fence, and that write must fail closed if a successor took the slot.

`allocateWriterEpoch` uses `EpochMintPolicy::NormalMount` by default and, on an absent epoch object, requires an authoritative `probeSentinelRaw` result of `KeyAbsent` before minting; `Present`, `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, and `Indeterminate` fail closed.

`EpochMintPolicy::DecommissionRecovery` permits re-minting over a surviving mount only when that mount is terminal, refuses a live member with `ABORTED`, and mints `max(1, surviving.writer_epoch + 1)` so the new epoch is distinct.
The epoch-presence probe is paid only on the absent-epoch branch; when the epoch object is present, the normal CAS bump does not probe the mount key.

`SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` continues after transient renewal failures while the confirmed lease deadline remains safe, but a definite `PreconditionFailed` mismatch always stops the loop and routes to `onRenewFailed` and self-remount recovery.

Phase A classifies same-uuid/same-epoch/unfenced as `same_epoch_state_uncertain` with `ABORTED`, same-uuid/different-epoch as `superseded` with `ABORTED`, foreign uuid as `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and absent body as `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.

If startup materialization grace consumes the claim TTL, `mountWritable` must redo one fresh conditional claim before arming the write fence; sane grace values shorter than `TTL − safety margin` incur no redo.

On the absent-epoch path, `NormalMount` proceeds only for authoritative `KeyAbsent`, rejects a present mount as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and fails closed for `ContainerAbsent`, `AccessDenied`, or `Indeterminate` probe outcomes.

`DecommissionRecovery` is used only by `openForDecommission`; it refuses a live surviving mount and mints an epoch distinct from a terminal surviving mount using `max(1, surviving_mount.writer_epoch + 1)`.
`ownsNamespace` is required for confirm routing because a pool UUID is shared across server roots and cannot by itself select the answering mount.

`ForeignMountDeath` classifies a foreign mount slot as `Absent`, `CleanFarewell`, `GcFenced`, `ObservedStable`, or `Live`; only the first four provide a certificate usable by the opt-in force-claim path.

`proveForeignMountDead` never treats `expires_at_ms <= now_ms` alone as proof of death; absent, farewell, and GC-fenced slots decide immediately, while other slots require an unchanged write token across `mountObservationThresholdMs(ttl_ms, poll_interval_ms)` on the observer's monotonic clock.

The force-claim write order is read-only death proof, token-conditional owner overwrite, unchanged `allocateWriterEpoch`, exact-token deletion of the stale mount slot, and then ordinary `claimMount`; deleting the slot before epoch allocation would disarm the guard against re-minting `writer_epoch 1`.
The ordinary `claimMount` invariant remains unchanged: a different `server_uuid` is `ForeignOwner` and must not be written over, regardless of expiry or prior state.
The mount claim protects writer identity, writer epochs, live double starts, the local write fence, and the mount's in-flight builds from GC; it does not provide a stable reader view.
`proveForeignMountDead` returns `Live` when a foreign holder's token keeps changing across the bounded observation restarts; the force path must throw `ABORTED` and write nothing in that case.

Force-claim preserves the durable monotone writer epoch by running `allocateWriterEpoch` before deleting the stale mount slot; it then deletes the slot with `deleteExact` using the observed token and invokes unmodified `claimMount`.

A force-claim permanently reassigns pool identity: the original server presents its old uuid on restart and is refused by `claimOwnerOrThrow` until the owner object is restored or `server_root_id` is reconfigured.

A wedged ref lane stores its admission fence generation, and each later caller's flush performs at most one bounded same-key, same-bytes conditional create under that generation; there is no background deadline-resetting retry loop.

The ref catalog at `cas/ref_catalog` maps each logical namespace to `Creating`, `Live`, or `Removing` plus a random 128-bit `incarnation`; the incarnation is the opaque `life_id` carried by every life-owned stream and state key.
Namespace lifecycle transitions are `Creating → Live → Removing → absent`; there is no fourth state and no pruning finalizer.

Runtime identity is scoped to `(life_id, admitted_fence_generation)`; a name slot is only a cache, and predecessor invalidation may detach only the matching runtime without clearing or rebinding a successor runtime.

`CatalogLifecycleReconciler` owns catalog lifecycle reconciliation and returns orthogonal `AuthorityStatus::{Authoritative,FencedOut}`, `CatalogResolution::{DrainComplete,ExactRowAbsent,ExactRowReplaced,ExactRowStillPresent}`, and exact `retired_lives`; unreadable resolution throws without producing a result.

After pool bootstrap, an absent or undecodable `cas/ref_catalog` is `CORRUPTED_DATA` and stops creation, removal, and GC; only bootstrap may create the empty catalog, and it may never be treated as virgin state again.

A server root owns live namespace work if and only if the mandatory catalog contains a `Creating`, `Live`, or `Removing` logical name under that root; opaque stream/state debris alone must not block owner or epoch recreation, and an unreadable catalog fails closed.

A same-name birth is refused with typed retry-later while its predecessor is `Removing`; the window includes the terminal fold and the next invocation's pre-fold drain, but no physical cleanup or pruning round.
The catalog remains bounded by `Creating + Live + Removing` entries under create/drop churn; stalled creators retain entries until fence-terminal reconciliation.

Creation uses catalog `Creating`, `_ckpt` create, and catalog `Live` conditional writes; publication from `Creating` is structurally impossible because only a `Live` life-minting resolution supplies a writer life.
Mode 1 timestamps the fence trip and remount completion with `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`; the duration excludes wall-clock changes from NTP steps and includes VM suspension.

The Mode 2 expiry detector runs at a durable-write admission refusal, not on the hot `mayMutate` read path; it atomically records the true `deadline_boot_ms` once per episode when `lost == false` and the deadline has passed.
Mode 1 and Mode 2 fence counters are disjoint: `tripMountLost` sets `lost = true`, while Mode 2 detection requires `lost == false`, so one fence window is counted as exactly one mode.

`CasMountRuntime::waitForWriteGrace` is a bounded, event-driven wait that returns immediately when `write_grace_ms == 0` or `mayMutate()` is true, and otherwise returns on fence re-arm, timeout, teardown, shutdown, or terminal lifecycle.

The write-grace wait uses a dedicated `write_grace_cv` and `write_grace_mutex`, never the remount, build, or ref-ledger locks; its predicate is `mayMutate() || remount_shutting_down || remountTerminal()`.

The grace condition variable is notified by `setMountDeadline` for Mode 2 re-arm, `armMountFence` for Mode 1 re-arm, teardown/shutdown transitions, and terminal transitions including `enterVanished`, `enterIdentityLost`, and `publishVanishedIntent`.

The plain-object write surface inserts `pool->waitForWriteGrace()` immediately before `admitted_generation = pool->fenceGeneration()`; the mid-operation generation checks in `CasPartWriteTxn.cpp:705` and `:747` remain immediate abort points.

The ref-log append surface waits before acquiring `ref_queue_mutex` or setting `leader_active`; placing the wait inside append-leader tenure would deadlock remount and shutdown drains that require every lane to be `!leader_active`.
The write-grace wait has a hard ceiling of `write_grace_ms` even if no remount or lifecycle signal arrives, and terminal or shutdown predicates unblock it promptly rather than waiting for the bound.

The fence/remount design does not change lease TTL, fence arming, generation bumping, self-remount, claim semantics, or the fence-not-rescue behavior; it adds only logging/counters and an optional client-side wait.
A self-remount cannot re-arm its fence while recovery is in flight: it cancels and joins recovery, or joins its completion, so no old-generation `_ckpt` CAS or install follows re-arm.

Decommission enumerates a claimed server root's catalog entries exactly, resumes unfinished `Removing` writer work under the claimed fence when `_ckpt` exists, leaves completed removal to GC, and performs a final exact catalog token check before slot retirement.
Recovery installation and wedge retries are guarded by the fence generation captured at recovery start; a successor seal conclusively rejects an old-generation retry.

A decommissioned server-root slot cannot retire while any catalog entry owned by that root remains; a `Removing` entry without a terminal record is resumable writer work when `_ckpt` exists and is corruption when `_ckpt` is absent.

At self-remount, the replacement writer epoch must satisfy `writer_epoch > mount_runtime.liveWriterEpoch()` before installation; a durable monotone epoch counter makes this an asserted fail-close precondition.
The sender evaluates relink conditions in fence-first order: mount fence, residency and recovery, wedge, apply state, then the committed ref row; any failure before the row yields `Unknown`.
A `Foreign` occupant causes `WedgeResolveCorrupted` to clear the marker while retaining the wedge; `CorruptFenceReaction` is a separate later action that closes the mount fence.

`NamespaceLifeId { RootNamespace ns; UInt128 incarnation; }` must qualify both ref objects and namespace files, reject zero incarnation, have no default construction, use canonical fixed-width lowercase hex, and be constructible only from a catalog entry or held live handle.
Once a namespace catalog entry is removed, files from that incarnation are structurally unreachable, so namespace rebirth need not wait for `_files` to become physically empty.
`Creating` namespaces are not recovered or published; `Live` and `Removing` namespaces require a readable `_ckpt` with `life_epoch`; a missing required `_ckpt` is corruption.
`Closed` and `Faulted` are terminal for one runtime and cannot be reopened by a test-only generation change; only a real remount replaces the runtime.

The named Stage B recovery state machine is `Creating`, `Live`, and `Removing`; after GC deletes a proved-complete `Removing` row, recovery has no namespace to resume and the janitor owns any surviving `_ckpt`.
Only the owning writer or a successor that has claimed and fenced the same server root may append `RemoveNamespace`; GC must never invent the terminal record.

Decommission selects victim namespaces by exact catalog ownership with no LIST fallback; `Removing` with `_ckpt` resumes the terminal append, `Removing` without `_ckpt` is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and a proved-complete `Removing` row remains GC-owned.
Decommission retirement is forbidden while any catalog entry owned by the server root remains; after entry absence, surviving opaque `_ckpt` and life objects are janitor debris.

`ContentAddressedTransaction::writeFile` classifies table-level files through `parseTableFilePath` and writes them with `putNamespaceFile`; other paths use a server-root-qualified `putMountpointObject` key.
Loose mountpoint objects use `roots/<server_root_id>/<path>` and carry no namespace, catalog row, life id, or later namespace-name resolution, so same-name namespace rebirth cannot retarget them.
The heartbeat is not safety-critical for lease fencing: `NoEpochCollision` remains green with `EnableHeartbeat = FALSE`, while the heartbeat is load-bearing for `NoFalseSteal`.

After a genuine post-wipe condition `epoch = 0 /\ epochCeiling > 0`, `RemintEpoch` may re-mint only when no live unfenced mount for the actor exists, while `RemintEpochDecom` requires a crashed actor and a Drift-aware terminal surviving mount unless `SabDecomBlindBypass` is enabled.

The v9 recovery and wedge paths must recheck the captured mount-fence generation immediately before every mutation: `slot-occupy`, `_ckpt` publication, install, unwedge, or equivalent retry publication.

The production strict ordering allocates the durable writer epoch before claiming the mount, as documented at `CasStore.cpp:312-316`; the model constraint is `StrictOrderMount == mount = None /\ mount.epoch > 0`.
`CaRefLaneCore` models six ownership states: `Ready`, `Writing`, `Wedged`, `NeedsRecovery`, `Closed`, and `Faulted`.
A captured predecessor runtime remains owned by its handle while the non-authoritative logical-name slot may publish a distinct successor after removal/rebirth or same-life self-remount.

Write and resolver operations must capture runtime provenance: `StartWrite` stores `lane_runtime` in `attempt_runtime`, `BeginResolve` carries it into `resolver_runtime`, and observations record `observation_runtime`.
The reference lane validates per-runtime projections of `cache_id` and `durable_id` during write, install, observation, resolution, and recovery transitions.
Immutable object producer fences are separate from checkpoint-CAS admission fences; after a remount, the current writer may checkpoint exactly one valid old-fence successor at `frontier + 1`.
A sender instance that loses the mount fence or current-writer authority must cause confirm to return `unknown`.
An unresolved every-attempt grant remains an in-memory duty while the mount lives and cannot be retired.

The v9 mount recovery layer captures `(actor, generation, op)` identity at admission and rechecks generation after I/O before every publication; an `Occupied` `slot-occupy` result must be resolved by comparing bytes.
A recovery result returning after self-remount is refused, and a dead lane's conditional create cannot be admitted under a successor generation.

The FORGET-only disk lifecycle is one-way: terminal states imply a latched fence, GC is destroyed and unrestartable, a started FORGET completes under fairness, and the GC scheduler eventually stops ticking after `Vanished`.

A server root is a single-writer mount slot identified by `server_root_id`, with lease and writer-epoch fencing stored at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/{owner,epoch,mount}`; a fenced writer cannot mutate the pool using stale state.
S13 requires that a stale GC leader cannot delete after losing the lease or fence race and that abandoned precommits do not grow without bound.
`WatermarkKeeper` maintains per-server single-writer liveness and an in-flight-build floor, while `HeartbeatKeeper` maintains per-build liveness and gates debris reclaim.

`WatermarkKeeper` holds a non-owning raw `Store*` back-reference and `ContentAddressedTransaction` holds a non-owning `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage&`; these are lifetime contracts rather than cycles.
In `system.cas_gc_log`, `server_root_id` identifies the mount whose GC scheduler ran the round and correlates with `system.cas_mounts`.
`system.cas_mounts` exposes one row per mount slot visible in the CAS backend at query time, including mounts belonging to other servers or other `server_root_id` values on the same server.
`system.cas_mounts` records `server_uuid`, `writer_epoch`, `renewal_sequence`, lease start and expiry, and `min_active_build_sequence`; `UINT64_MAX` for the last means the mount said farewell.
The `system.cas_mounts` `state` value is one of `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.
The `system.cas_mounts` `gc_fenced` column is `1` when GC has terminally fenced the slot.
The revised slot operation uses one raw conditional create, at most one raw exact GET, caller-side byte adjudication, and per-outcome backend operation-count assertions
Self-remount recovery must add cancellation polling at I/O boundaries and a cancel-or-join barrier before fence rearm, after which no old _ckpt or install mutation may follow
OwnerProto at <prefix>/gc/server-roots/<srid>/owner is a sticky binding from server_root_id to server UUID and prevents silent reuse under a different UUID
ServerEpochProto provides durable monotone writer-epoch allocation so a fenced writer cannot reuse the same epoch after reopen
MountLeaseProto is live lease and ack-floor state, not identity; server identity belongs to OwnerProto
The per-object evolution gates are v <= G_BUILD, a pool min_reader_generation forward floor and backward format floor at mount, and a future roster-based fleet floor designed but not yet built
Breaking v3 changes use a version-keyed encoder ladder that writes the field set valid at the pool floor, and the floor raise fences old binaries at mount
Only the owning mounted writer or a successor that has claimed and fenced the server root may append an interrupted terminal removal record; ordinary GC must not append it.

Recovery must capture the mount fence generation at admission and require the same generation plus a non-superseded runtime for every slot-occupy, _ckpt CAS, and final install; remount must cancel or wait for recovery before rearming.
Creating reconciliation must bind the entry to creator mount identity or fence generation, wait for that authority to become terminal, and CAS-delete only an unchanged catalog token.

Every namespace-scoped CAS operation should use a typed NamespaceHandle{namespace, incarnation, local_life_generation} through Pool, CasPlainObjects, PartWriteTxn, ref recovery/publishing, cleanup, and upper metadata operations.

A decommissioned server-root slot must not retire while any catalog entry owned by that root remains, and a claimed successor must enumerate catalog entries exactly and resume Removing entries without a terminal record.

A ref-append wedge must retain the admitted fence generation and allow each foreground lane flush at most one bounded controller operation with that generation; unresolved outcomes retain the wedge for a later caller or remount.

Decommission must recover and append the missing terminal under its claimed fence when _ckpt is present, and when _ckpt is absent it must exact-CAS-remove the catalog entry or fail as corruption if finalization ordering cannot be established.
If an old append CAS commits before recovery fencing, recovery rereads and adopts the node; if the fence commits first, the old CAS is permanently invalid because its expected token is stale.
Physical emptiness is not a rebirth precondition because old objects are incarnation-qualified; omitted old objects are retained rather than guessed dead after the catalog entry is removed.
`RootNamespace` has no constructor taking a `NamespaceLifeId`; the explicitness of its `String` constructor is unrelated to constructibility from `NamespaceLifeId`.
A persisted `CreatorFence.fence_generation` is not comparable across processes because it is a process-local `std::atomic<uint64_t>` whose counter restarts at zero in another `CasMountRuntime`.
`probeNonTerminalMountSlots` treats an absent mount slot as nothing to hold and an undecodable slot body as held; its conservative precedent applies only to the undecodable-body case.
`RefTableRuntime::life` has two writers: `ensureRefTableRecovered` during recovery and step 1 of `namespaceFilesLifeIfReadable`, which can resolve it without recovery.
The mount write-fence deadline uses `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, and expired-mount reclaim requires observing a stable holder token for a full `TTL + Drift` window on the reclaimer's own monotonic clock.
`SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` refuses and raises an exception, regardless of `FORCE`, when another GC leader holds the disk lease.

`SYSTEM CAS DROP POOL MEMBER 'server_root_id' FROM DISK 'disk_name' [ON CLUSTER cluster_name]` permanently decommissions a dead content-addressed pool member by claiming its mount slot as an administrative writer, fencing that `server_root_id`, dropping its table namespaces, draining eligible debris, and retiring the slot after confirmed drains.

decommissionPoolMember re-reads the catalog for each selected entry and requires exact structural equality with the selected CatalogEntry; a same-name row with a changed incarnation is rejected with CORRUPTED_DATA.

Retirement of a pool-member slot is forbidden while any catalog entry owned by that root remains, including an entry transitioned from Live to Removing during the same decommission call; cleanup proceeds in two phases with GC between the calls.

The decommission retirement tail refuses a stale ownership cut when fresh_retirement_catalog.token != retirement_catalog_cut->token or fresh_retirement_catalog.catalog != retirement_catalog_cut->catalog, reporting catalog changed after the victim ownership check; refusing slot retirement against a stale cut.

The system.cas_mounts columns are started_at and expires_at; the _ms suffix remains on internal MountLease millisecond fields, persisted "sat"/"eat" body keys, cas-inspect JSON keys, holder_expires_at_ms, and log fields because those values are raw epoch milliseconds rather than DateTime64(3) columns.

The 05012_cas_mounts_typed_columns.reference remains unchanged because the query orders expires_at, server_uuid, and started_at in the same alphabetical order as the old names; a missing renamed column would reduce the result from three rows to two and fail the reference.

`MountLease` fields and related `system.cas_log` detail keys retain `started_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` because their values are raw epoch milliseconds; the suffix is semantically accurate even where a display column uses `DateTime64(3)`.

`seedCompletedRemoving` recovers and retains the predecessor runtime while its catalog row is `Live`; absent and replacement fence-race fixtures therefore exercise real `Pool::invalidateRemovedCatalogLife` behavior and force name-based recovery away from the predecessor life.
The immutable runtime identity has the shape `RootNamespace -> RefNameSlot -> RefTableRuntime(NamespaceLifeId, admitted_fence_generation)`.

`RefTableRuntime::life` and `RefTableRuntime::admitted_fence_generation` are construction-only const values; a name slot is a non-authoritative current-pointer cache whose predecessor can be detached while external `shared_ptr` holders keep it alive.
